- Portfolio of value-added and environmentally compliant products that has supported margin expansion and enabled presence in Southeast Asia, Africa and Europe

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical conflict and the resulting commodity and logistics shock — Management calls global uncertainty the new normal, driven by the Russia-Ukraine and Gaza wars and the ongoing Iran-Israel conflict; these have significantly impacted commodity and logistics markets, causing sharp increases in crude oil and freight costs and exposing global supply chains to continuous disruption. Mitigation is dual sourcing, proactive market monitoring and strategic planning.
- Feedstock dependence and pricing - naphtha, imported LPG and propane — India remains heavily dependent on naphtha as a feedstock along with imported LPG and propane for downstream chemical production, exposing the industry to global crude, naphtha and LPG price fluctuations. Feedstock availability and pricing will remain a key constraint until India develops access to more affordable domestic gaseous hydrocarbons at scale.
- Structural cost disadvantage versus ethane-advantaged regions — The naphtha/LPG dependency creates cost sensitivities and competitive disadvantages compared to regions like the United States, where access to ethane-rich shale gas provides a structural cost advantage - a durable margin headwind for Indian downstream chemical producers.
- Prolonged global chemical industry slowdown and margin compression — The global chemical industry has faced a slowdown since 2022 driven by capacity imbalances and weaker demand across key sectors; after two decades of rapid expansion the industry is recalibrating expectations, with lower margins and reduced value creation becoming the new reality.
- Chinese overstocking and oversupply — Significant overstocking and oversupply from China is named as a driver of the industry slowdown, pressuring pricing and demand across key chemical sectors.
- Raw material price volatility and supply-chain constraints — FY2025-26 was marked by trade disruptions, supply chain constraints, inflationary pressures and volatility in key raw material markets; the Company relies on multipurpose manufacturing facilities that allow it to pivot using alternate raw materials, and on long term off-take agreements, to absorb this.
- Rising regulatory and compliance cost from the policy environment — Management notes the policy environment presents a dual impact - while offering fiscal and strategic support for growth through FDI policies, PLI schemes, PCPIR clusters and decarbonization initiatives, it also introduces higher compliance costs for companies.
- Industry cyclicality and liquidity exposure — Management explicitly maintains strict liquidity to navigate industry cycles, indicating cycle-driven earnings and working-capital risk in a downcycle.

business.body: The Company is domiciled in India with its registered office in Mumbai and is engaged in the manufacturing of specialty chemicals, with manufacturing carried out from plants at Dahej (Gujarat) and Kurkumbh, District Pune (Maharashtra). It has decades of experience in specialty chemicals including surfactants and performance additives, and has built customer relationships across textiles, agrochemicals, personal care and oilfield chemicals. Its technical expertise and manufacturing capabilities, particularly in oilfield chemicals and polymer additives, position it as a quality-focused supplier in performance chemicals, and it serves both domestic and export markets.

outlook.body:
- Mitigate raw-material and supply-chain risk through dual sourcing and proactive market monitoring backed by strategic planning
- Use multipurpose manufacturing facilities to pivot to alternate raw materials as market conditions require
- Use long term off-take agreements commercially to stabilize the chain between suppliers and customers
- Maintain strict liquidity financially in order to navigate industry cycles
- Leverage AI and digital tools to enhance data analysis and decision-making
- The routed governance sections do not set out a dividend or payout policy. The stated capital-allocation intent is reinvestment into the manufacturing and innovation base: management describes FY2025-26 as a year of investment across operations, technology and the product portfolio to strengthen competitive position, with a key milestone being the expansion of ethoxylation capacity through the addition of a new EO reactor at the Dahej facility - framed as a strategic investment that strengthens the manufacturing platform, enhances operational flexibility and broadens the range of specialty chemical applications served. Alongside this, the Company continued to modernise production infrastructure, strengthen manufacturing systems, and invest in application development and customer-focused innovation, including the commissioning of a dedicated Agrochemical Application Laboratory. Governance framing is that good corporate governance leads to long term shareholder value; CSR spending became applicable during FY2025-26 because net profit exceeded the prescribed statutory threshold in the preceding financial year, and the Board modified the CSR Policy on August 7, 2025.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's central expansion move is the doubling of capacity in its major area of operation, Ethoxylation, with the expanded capacity directed towards some of its major oilfield initiatives - management frames this as delivering both growth and a competitive advantage. During FY2025-26 the Company progressed these capacity expansion initiatives, including enhancement of ethoxylation capabilities and strengthening of manufacturing infrastructure to support future growth, alongside operational efficiency gains from better process controls, energy optimization and reduction in non-standard batch materials. On the innovation side, the Company established an Application Development laboratory in the agriculture chemicals space to strengthen customer-centric product development and commercialization, and has started working on logistics and procurement initiatives based on AI. No commissioning date, project cost or dated completion timeline for the ethoxylation expansion is disclosed in the routed sections.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global chemical industry has faced a slowdown since 2022 driven by capacity imbalances, weaker demand across key sectors, and significant overstocking and oversupply from China; the industry is recalibrating to lower margins and reduced value creation as the new reality
- Petrochemicals have emerged as the primary driver of growth in global oil and gas demand and are expected to remain the dominant source of future oil demand growth as demand for traditional fuels plateaus
- Demand for plastics and synthetic materials used in construction, packaging, automotive and other industries has accelerated the petrochemical demand trend
- Global uncertainty has become the new normal on the back of the Russia-Ukraine and Gaza wars and the Iran-Israel conflict, driving sharp increases in crude oil and freight costs and continuous supply-chain disruption
- India's dependence on naphtha feedstock plus imported LPG and propane exposes the industry to global crude, naphtha and LPG price swings and creates a competitive disadvantage versus regions such as the United States with ethane-rich shale gas
- Feedstock availability and pricing will remain a key constraint until India develops access to more affordable domestic gaseous hydrocarbons at scale
- 2025 has emerged as a pivotal year for the Indian chemical sector, with strategic government policies catalyzing investments and shifting focus toward high complexity and value-added segments
- The Company utilises long term off-take agreements to stabilize the chain between suppliers and customers (qualitative; no order-book value disclosed in this section)
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
